subject: Cognitive Science
title: Categorization Under Pressure
description: A micro-lesson that makes Categorization Under Pressure usable.

hook.text: A doctor in the ER has seconds to classify symptoms. Fast categorization can save a life.

buildup.text: Under time pressure, people rely more on surface similarity and less on deep causal reasoning.

discovery.text: Rushed participants classify a bat as a bird more often—it looks and flies like one.

twist.text: Experts resist this shift. Trained radiologists still spot rare patterns under stress.

climax.text: Deep knowledge makes categorization automatic, freeing it from time pressure's distortions.

punchline.text: Hurry makes you think in shortcuts.

quiz.question: How does time pressure affect categorization?
options: People rely more on surface similarity
